key_insight: Parameter-specific sparsity lets a learned controller measure only the qubit-wise commuting groups most relevant to variational quantum gradients.
engineering_relevance: Selective measurement can reduce VQE shot requirements while retaining energy accuracy close to measuring all QWC groups.
method: Characterize how gradient-contribution relevance varies across parameters and optimization states.
Predict group relevance from Hamiltonian, circuit, light-cone, and current-state features.
Select measurements using a tunable coverage threshold, with exact contributions needed only for offline supervision.
evidence_signal: Across 15 molecular VQE settings, the method saved 49.6% of nominal gradient-measurement shots with a mean absolute energy gap of 5.67 mHa relative to Full-QWC.
watch_item: The reported savings concern nominal measurement shots; end-to-end runtime benefits and generalization beyond the evaluated settings remain to be established.
paper_title: Variational Relevance-Informed Sparsification of Term Measurements for Variational Quantum Algorithms
